A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same ABC paper. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original accuracy, inference-cost, and deployment experiments in Section 5, plus threshold, selection-rate, and cascade analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experimental and simulation results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 3–4 retain the same ensemble cascade, voting-based and score-based deferral rules, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Table 2 retains the same nine datasets and tasks. The edge-to-cloud, heterogeneous-GPU, and black-box API evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain WoC and best single models, plus FrugalGPT, AutoMix+T, AutoMix+P, and MoT LLM Cascade in the API experiments.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings, metrics, model configurations, and four-shot API prompting are unchanged. Section 4.4 changes '100' validation samples to '∼100', consistent with Appendix B's existing 'around 100' description; no different sample budget is specified.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendices B, C, and E retain the same threshold-stability, selection-rate, parallelization, relative-cost, and cascade-configuration analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical estimation and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. No run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run summaries are added.

E6.justification: The reported curves, findings, and numerical entries are unchanged. For example, Table 5 retains CIFAR-10 GPU costs of $0.79/hour for ABC and $2.49/hour for the best single model.

T1.justification: Definitions 4.1 and A.1, Proposition 4.1, its Appendix A proof, the risk derivations, and Appendix B's threshold estimator are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free cascading contribution, drop-in replacement claims, and accuracy and cost-saving claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations and qualifications concerning ensemble overhead, parallelization, cost disparities, open-ended generation, and potential bias in majority voting.

D1.justification: The model specifications, pricing information, threshold-estimation instructions, and baseline implementation details are unchanged. The approximate sample-count wording adds nothing beyond the existing Appendix B disclosure.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the positioning relative to prior cascading methods are unchanged. The new acknowledgements do not introduce cited research or revise novelty claims.

P1.justification: V4 adds an Acknowledgements section identifying contributors and funding, makes one sample-count phrase approximate, and updates the version/date stamp. The substantive narrative and organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Takeaway boxes have slightly tighter spacing, text reflows on pages 10–14, and acknowledgements occupy additional space on page 14. All figures, tables, and the algorithm retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: V4 adds contributor and funding disclosure and aligns the sample-count summary with the existing Appendix B description. These limited administrative and presentation refinements leave the paper's scientific support, reproducibility, and substantive clarity essentially unchanged.
